srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

podcast.body: Released in the fall of 2003, "Mr. Brightside" is one of the 21st century's biggest songs, demonstrating incredible staying power, especially in the UK where it's charted for over 450 weeks. It has been streamed nearly 2.5 billion times on Spotify, won numerous awards, and is a staple at sporting events, generating millions for The Killers. The song's origin traces back to Brandon Flowers' heartbreak as a 19-year-old, after he saw his ex-girlfriend with another man at The Crown and Anchor bar in Las Vegas, leading him to furiously write down his spiraling imaginations of their actions later that night, attempting to put on a brave face by calling himself "Mr. Brightside." The music was already written by guitarist Dave Keuning, and their crude demo with a drum machine helped them secure a record deal. "As Brandon has said, who knows that betrayal could sound so good."

podcast.body: The Killers' debut single, based on singer Brandon Flowers seeing an old girlfriend with a new guy in a bar in his hometown of Las Vegas. The song was first released on September 29, 2003, and later appeared on the "Hot Fuss" album. It initially performed poorly but, upon its re-release in 2004, achieved massive global success, particularly in the UK, where it became the third biggest selling and streaming song of all time, surpassed only by Oasis and Ed Sheeran. It holds the record as the longest-charting single in British singles charts history, spending over 408 weeks (nearly seven and a half years) in the ranking, with a streak of over 15 years constantly on the charts. It was named Song of the Decade multiple times and became the most streamed song on Spotify in the UK and Ireland in the 2000s, selling millions of copies. Despite its immense popularity and enduring appeal, "Mr. Brightside" surprisingly never reached number one on many major singles charts. "The song first came out on September 29, 2003 and would later appear on the Hot Fuss album."
